newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PacDun sees higher year net profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PacDun sees higher year net profit.

text.p: Diversified manufacturer Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Friday that it believed it would achieve its previous forecast of a higher profit for the full year to June 30, 1996 than a year earlier.

"Assuming there is no further deterioration in market conditions, the directors believe their previous forecast that the full year result will exceed the previous year, will be achieved," Pacific Dunlop said in releasing its first half results.

Earlier, Pacific Dunlop reported a 30.2 percent fall in pre-tax operating profit to A$128.4 million for the six months to December, while net profit fell 27.6 percent to A$84.5 million. There were no abnormals. It cut its interim dividend to seven cents per share from 11 cents.
Pacific Dunlop said sales from its continuing businesses fell to A$2.9 billion from A$3.0 billion in the comparable half year.
"The reduction is mainly due to the effect of the stronger Australian dollar against the U.S. dollar and European currencies," Pacific Dunlop said.
"This particularly impacted our GNB Technologies and Ansell International Groups," it said.
GNB Technologies' operating profit fell to A$1 million from A$45 million a year earlier.

"GNB had a disappointing result reflecting heavy one-off costs associated in part with modifications to the Columbus lead smelter in the United States and the resultant restriction on production throughput," Pacific Dunlop said.
"The smelter's major problems have been addressed and production output is progressively improving to more satisfactory levels," it said.

Pacific Dunlop's Ansell International division posted a six month operating profit of A$54 million, up from A$52 million a year earlier, due in part to the successful launch of its powder-free medical glove products.
Pacific Dunlop said the Australian markets for its various units remained disappointingly subdued.
"However initiatives taken by the company should enable further restoration of margins in the period ahead," it said.
"All business are now firmly focused on margin improvement, inventory reduction and more rigorous disciplines on return on capital."
The lower GNB Technologies profit included a A$12.3 million one-off assset write-down for obsolete equipment and scrapped facilities.
"Sales in the second half are expected to improve with the addition of the large U.S. retail chain Montgomery Ward as a new customer," Pacific Dunlop said of GNB Technologies.
Pacific Dunlop's shares were up one cent at A$3.14 at 3.15 p.m. (0415 GMT).
